newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco class-action campaign to start in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco class-action campaign to start in Florida.

text.p: Lawyers pressing a Florida class-action suit against cigarette makers on Wednesday begin a three-month publicity campaign to notify Florida smokers and their survivors of their legal rights.
The suit, which is scheduled for trial in September in Dade County Court here, claims damages for state residents who fell ill or died from illnesses due to a smoking addiction.

According to a spokesman for Stanley Rosenblatt, the lawyer bringing the Florida suit, the publicity campaign will include television and radio commercials, ads in newspapers throughout Florida and a mass mailing to Florida physicians.
A toll-free number, which has not been selected, will also be announced.
A news conference has been scheduled for 1000 EST/1500 GMT on Wednesday by Rosenblatt and Howard Engle, a physician who is the lead plaintiff in the suit.

All Florida residents and their survivors with potential claims against Philip Morris Cos Inc ., RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp and other tobacco companies will be included in the Engle class-action suit unless they notify Rosenblatt that they want to be kept out, the spokesman said.

The Engle claim is the first to be scheduled for trial of a flurry of a anti-tobacco class-action suits making their way through U.S. courts. A smaller class-action by U.S. flight attendants claiming harm from inhaling second-hand smoke on passenger jets is set to begin June 2 in Miami.

At least 10 state actions have grown out of a national class-action suit filed in a federal court in New Orleans but dismissed last year because the potentially millions of claims were judged to be too many to be handled in one trial.
